letters.title: On the club's social media and website
letters.subject: Two further questions, after another inappropriate post
letters.note: Reproduced exactly as sent. A screenshot of the post that prompted it was attached to the email and is not republished here: the point is the process that let it out, not the post itself. The two questions in this letter are additional to the ten from the consultation and are not outputs of it - they were agreed by the KTFCSA working group.

body.x: Good afternoon,

Further to my earlier email/open letter, I'd like to share a perfect example of how the club is currently conducting its social media presence, despite the numerous and serious continuous misuse which has a direct impact on the perception of our club.
I have attached the latest faux pas as a screenshot.
171 out of 199 (85.9%) of survey respondents feel the club communications are sub-par.
I'd really appreciate it if you could also confirm through which means the social media aspect is being improved.

For consistency, we'd really appreciate an answer the following questions in addition to the ten. These questions are not direct outputs of the aforementioned survey, but have been agreed by the KTFCSA working group and shared, as is, on social media and our website.

Despite previous statements from the club and a newly-appointed dedicated Social Media Manager, the club's digital presence is (subjectively) so poor. I appreciate it's a new role and a learning curve, however, this does not excuse yet another inappropriate post shared by club. What, if any, peer checking or approval process is in place to ensure public-facing content is accurate and appropriate?

The website is not being maintained and is out of date too. For example, the Officials page is incredibly inaccurate and contains the names of people (six, just at a first glance), who may not wish to be associated with the club. When, and how, will this be addressed and who is responsible for maintaining the official club website?

In 2026, digital presence is so incredibly important to get right, consistently. I also appreciate it's incredibly difficult to carry it out perfectly, however the errors are continually repeated to the point that now anecdotally, many feel it's actively detrimental and damaging to the club's 151-year-old brand.
Thank you - appreciate your time,

letters.note: Reproduced exactly as sent, including the wording. The questions and figures in it are the same ones published on this page.

body.x: Dear George / KTFC Board,

I hope you are well. I am writing on behalf of the newly-forming Kettering Town FC Supporters' Association, a working group of supporters looking to help wade through the noise of social media to capture fan sentiment through hard and consistent data.

Our website, fans.ktfcsa.com, should give you a good overview of what we are looking to achieve and some of the features and functionalities built for fans, by fans. Our work is very carefully focused around trying to amplify fan voices while being very mindful of the good work done by the Trust.

Between Monday 17 and midday on Friday 21 August we asked Kettering Town supporters what they make of the way the club is being run. 199 people answered in five days. Anyone could take part, with or without an account, one response per device. Nobody was paid, prompted or selected. The full results, every figure and the method behind them, are published at fans.ktfcsa.com and will stay there.
We are writing because we told supporters we would put what they said directly to the club, in writing, and publish whatever comes back.
1. What supporters said
Confidence in how the club is being run stands at 2.4 out of ten. When the same question was put to this fanbase in May, it was 8.1.

x: Lowest score of 1 out of 10: 96 people
Club heading in the wrong direction: 151 of 199
Club heading in the right direction: 9 of 199

body.x: The concerns are concentrated rather than scattered:
Asked how well each body represents them, supporters answered:

x: Club ownership: 83% poor or very poor
The club board: 71% poor or very poor
Club partners and sponsors: 53% poor or very poor

body.x: We would ask you not to read these as the usual noise. The same fanbase gave a score of 8.1 only three months ago.
2. What this is not
Two findings cut against the general mood and we publish them as plainly as the rest.

The team is the single most praised thing about the club, named by 168 of 199 supporters. The criticism here is aimed at how the club is run. It is not aimed at the players, the manager, or the staff who turn up every week.
The Supporters' Trust, whose role several supporters raised, is rated good or very good by more people than rate it poorly.

We have also held back eight submissions in full. Some carried allegations we are not in a position to stand up, and some were not appropriate to pass on. They have not been sent to you and they have not been published. That is not us protecting anyone. It is us keeping this to what can reasonably be answered.
3. The questions
Supporters submitted 109 questions. We have grouped them into the ten below. The wording of each is ours; the number beside it is how many supporters asked that question in one form or another.
The ten questions are listed in full above, each with the number of supporters who asked it and how long it has gone unanswered.
Addendum
Six questions did not fall under any of the above. They are reproduced here in supporters' own words so that nothing asked is left out.

x: How sustainable are the squad we have?
When will the club go back to being the club I went to watch twice a week, and love being part of.
What is the most important asset of a football club? If your answer is its Supporters, do you acknowledge that many of those Supporters are here due to the excellent work of Phil Wade?
What is the reason that George and his family are here?
Don't let us lose this once in a generation opportunity with Brad. Leave the club with your head held high after playoffs and FA Cup run.
When will the website be updated, do we not have anyone working on it?

body.x: 4. A reply
We would kindly ask for a reply by Friday 4 September 2026.

The results page publishes which of these questions have been answered and how long any unanswered question has been outstanding. That page updates itself. We would far rather it recorded answers than days.
5. What we would like to happen next

181 of the 199 supporters who answered said they would attend a first meeting of the Supporters' Association, 118 of them in person. That is the clearest single result in the whole exercise, and it is a constructive one. Supporters are not asking to run the club. They are asking to be told things.

For transparency, a copy of this open letter will be shared to the KTFC Supporters' Association website and social media pages shortly, alongside the full list of questions and the time and date sent.

We are aware that supporters have discussed forms of protest, and the report records what they said they would support, including 86 who backed a boycott. We report that because it is what the data shows. We are not calling for any of it, and we would much rather report that these questions were answered, and answered fully.
We would welcome a meeting or with the board, at a time of your choosing, and we would publish an account of it either way.

The Supporters' Association is independent of the club, takes no money from it, and speaks only for the supporters who answered. The group is in its infancy, but interest in the initiative has been encouraging, and we are now looking to arrange a first meeting in person.
We have no interest in a battle with Kettering Town Football Club. We have an interest in it being run well and a hope that the work being done can be leveraged to ultimately enhance fan experience.

x: On behalf of the newly-formed Kettering Town FC Supporters' Association working group

letters.title: On how the club is being run
letters.subject: The consultation, and ten questions

reply.from: George Akhtar and the KTFC Board
reply.note: The club replied a day inside the date we asked for. It is published here in full, unedited. It does not answer the twelve questions one by one, and we have said so against each of them, but it is a reply and it makes commitments we intend to hold them to.
commitments: To meet the Poppies Supporters Trust more regularly.
To bring the website and social media up to standard and keep them there.
To improve communication - monthly club updates across all streams, or a wider face to face fans forum.
reply.body:
Dear Danny

Thank you for taking the time to send this email to us and the results of your on-line survey.

You (your survey) poses many questions, and I hope that you can understand that we as a business cannot go into the level of detail that you have asked. We operate and are owned by a Limited Company which publish annual accounts and these are available for all to see. As a limited company, the strategy, direction and indeed set up of the club hierarchy is reviewed on a regular basis. This is not simply a look at how we are currently structured, but on “what do we need to move forward, today and tomorrow based on the evolving world that surrounds and informs us”.

As you are aware we are already having an on-going relationship with The Poppies Supporters Trust, who act as an independent body with its own membership, and which represents the fans. This has worked well over many years, and we are looking to meet more regularly as we feel that this helps provide an important link to the fans. Volunteers are key to any non-league football club, as without them, match days simply would not happen. However, volunteers change and move on for many different reasons and replacing them is not easy. If you look around at other football clubs and indeed other community-based groups/projects, you will see there is a huge volunteer need and a growing “need gap has formed”. We, ourselves, have advertised for many volunteer roles and the applications have not led to all positions being filled. This continues today.

We also acknowledge your comments on social media and the website; this is something that we are well aware of and are putting steps in place to bring this to the expected standard, that we and our fans would expect, and then to maintain going forward. Social media, as you indicate, is key in today’s world but I do remind you that no matter the content that we put out, there will always be “opposing views” as that is human nature.

We hope that the above shows a level of commitment and our desire to engage with fans. We will also look at improving communication going forward, be this through monthly club updates across all streams or a wider face to face/fans forum.

We trust that you and the supporters that you represent, will focus on the football being played on the pitch. We have a current “unbeaten” start to the season (at time of writing) and an exciting local derby against Wellingborough Town to look forward to in the first qualifying round of the FA Cup.

Yours

George Akhtar and KTFC Board

ourReply.from: Danny Jordan, on behalf of the Association
ourReply.body:
Dear George,

Thank you for taking the time to respond to my email; I'll share this with the working group and reflect our website & socials to confirm the club has responded, though in my opinion, not answered any question directly; which is of course within your rights.

I'll follow up, if relevant, with the outcome of our first face-to-face meeting on Monday.

Again; appreciate your time.

Kind regards,

Danny Jordan
Kettering Town FC Supporters' Association
